text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The army wants the Islamist employment minister charged for insulting the military after he criticised the actions of a military commander in a pro-Islamist district.

- Defence Minister Turhan Tayan said Turkey would act to block a Greek Cypriot attempt to buy anti-aircraft missiles from Russia. If necessary, this would be done by freezing out the Mediterranean island, as the U.S. did with Cuba in 1960.
- The ratings group Moodys says it could downgrade Turkey's credit rating.
- Parliament is due to discuss lifting the immunity of two government MPs in connection with a scandal over links between the state and the underworld.

- A report on state-underworld links is trying to cover up the magnitude of the affair by painting a picture of individual misdeeds by the odd leading personality and denying the existance of an organised gang within state ranks.

- Turkey wants to review rules about international passage through the Bosphorus straits in order to block a Greek Cypriot bid to buy anti-aircraft missiles from Russia. The missiles may be delivered by sea through the straits -- Russia's only outlet to the Mediterranean.
- Two surprise bidders for the privatisation of Erdemir, Turkey's biggest state-owned flat steel producer.
- Greek Cypriot government spokesman Yannakis Kasullides says in an interview that Greek Cyprus' planned anti-aircraft missile systems would not be used against Turkey.
